beats.intro: Chapter twenty-two. [[sub]]Two-phase locking, and its shadow: deadlock.
beats.ground: A library with one rulebook. [[room]]The reading room fits twenty readers at once. Nobody changes the book, so everybody reads. [[diary]]But the diary has one copy. One rewriter takes it home, and nineteen people wait. [[w]]Write this: many may read together; one writer excludes everyone.
beats.locks: Two lock modes, one grid. [[s]]S means shared, for reading. S plus S is fine. [[x]]X means exclusive, for writing. X against anything is a clash. [[w]]Write this: S with S ok; X with everything no.
beats.twopl: Two phases, one way through. [[grow]]Growing: grab locks, release none. [[point]]Lock point: the moment you hold everything you will ever hold. [[shrink]]Shrinking: release locks, grab none. Never regrow. [[safe]]This discipline guarantees serializability. It does not prevent deadlock. [[w]]Write this: grow, lock point, shrink; serializable yes, deadlock still possible.
beats.q1: Quick check. [[q]]In two-phase locking, what is forbidden after the first unlock?
beats.deadlock: Two transactions, two items, one circle. [[hold]]T1 holds A and waits for B. T2 holds B and waits for A. [[cycle]]Each waits for the other, forever. That circle is the deadlock. [[handle]]Handle it four ways: prevention, avoidance, detection with a wait-for graph, or timeout. Detection finds the circle; the cure aborts a victim and breaks it. [[w]]Write this: draw the holds-and-waits circle, name PADT, abort a victim.
beats.q2: Quick check. [[q]]Deadlock is detected using what?
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[w1]]S with S is fine; X clashes with everything. [[w2]]Grow, lock point, shrink, never regrow: serializable, but deadlock still possible. [[w3]]Deadlock is a holds-and-waits circle; find it with the wait-for graph, fix it by aborting a victim.
